title: Game Night Jeopardy — Level Up Edition
description: A millennial game night board covering late 90s/early 2000s video games, two rounds of iconic music from the 90s and early 2000s, watershed historical events, current events from 2024–2025, and legendary sports moments.

questions.question: Released for the Sony PlayStation in 1996 and developed by Naughty Dog, this marsupial platformer — known for his blue jeans and signature spin attack — served as Sony's unofficial rival to Nintendo's Mario throughout the late 90s.

Maxis and EA released this PC life-simulation game in February 2000, letting players design and micromanage virtual people's homes, jobs, and relationships — it became the best-selling PC game series in history.

In Hideo Kojima's 1998 PlayStation stealth thriller, a psychic villain read Snake's memory card to comment on other Konami games you had played — then forced players to plug their controller into the console's second port to land a hit on him.

This 1998 Valve first-person shooter — set in a research facility beneath the New Mexico desert after a catastrophic alien incident — pioneered narrative-driven level design without cutscenes and spawned a sequel that took six years to arrive.

Blizzard's 1998 real-time strategy title — pitting Terran, Zerg, and Protoss races against each other — became a national cultural institution in South Korea, where professional players trained in teams, competed in televised leagues, and earned celebrity status.

Released in 1995 from the album CrazySexyCool, this TLC track featured a rap verse from Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes and built its message around cautionary tales about HIV and drug violence — it topped the Billboard Hot 100.

This Canadian country-pop star's 1997 album Come On Over became one of the best-selling albums in music history, and its 1999 lead single urged women to shed their inhibitions and feel empowered to do whatever they want.

Billy Corgan's sweeping 1995 double album produced the Grammy-winning hard rock single 'Bullet With Butterfly Wings,' whose famous chorus declared 'Despite all my rage I am still just a rat in a cage.'
questions.answer: What is Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness?

questions.question: Gwen Stefani's ska-influenced California band released this 1996 breakup anthem — written about her split from bassist Tony Kanal — that spent 15 weeks at number one on Billboard's Adult Top 40 chart, a record until 1998.

Written for the 1998 Nicolas Cage film City of Angels, this John Rzeznik power ballad spent a then-record 18 weeks atop Billboard's Hot 100 Airplay chart — yet never officially charted on the Hot 100 itself, because no commercial single was released.

This 2002 Nelly smash, built on a sample from Chuck Brown's go-go classic 'Bustin' Loose,' invited everyone to take off their clothes, hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100, and won a Grammy for Best Male Rap Solo Performance.

This 2002 Eminem track — written for a semi-autobiographical film about a Detroit battle rapper — became the first hip-hop song to win the Academy Award for Best Original Song, urging its narrator to seize one moment of opportunity.

This 2004 Usher lead single, produced by Lil Jon and featuring a rap from Ludacris, sat at the top of the Billboard Hot 100 for 12 consecutive weeks — the year's longest-running number-one — helping Usher dominate the chart with four chart-toppers in a single calendar year.

This debut single from a British band formed at University College London arrived in 2000 with a spare fingerpicked guitar figure and a color-named title that lead singer Chris Martin spotted while flipping through a reference book in a recording studio.

Released on the morning of September 11, 2001, this Jay-Z album — featuring production from Kanye West and Just Blaze — is considered his finest work, with the celebratory lead single 'Izzo (H.O.V.A.)' contrasting the battle-rap assault of 'Takeover' on the same record.

Between 1995 and 2000, billions in venture capital poured into internet startups before this financial collapse wiped out trillions in wealth — the NASDAQ Composite eventually lost nearly 78% of its peak value by October 2002.

On June 26, 2000, President Clinton and British Prime Minister Tony Blair jointly announced that scientists had completed a working draft of this landmark scientific project — mapping the approximately 3 billion base pairs of human DNA.
questions.answer: What is the Human Genome Project?

questions.question: On October 3, 1995, a Los Angeles jury delivered a 'not guilty' verdict in this celebrity murder trial after nine months of testimony — the former NFL star had been charged with killing his ex-wife Nicole Brown and her friend Ron Goldman.

This 36-day constitutional crisis ended on December 12, 2000, when the U.S. Supreme Court halted Florida's ballot recount — effectively awarding the presidency by a margin of just 537 certified votes in a single decisive state.

On February 22, 1997, Scotland's Roslin Institute announced this Finn-Dorset sheep had been created from a single adult mammary gland cell, making her the first mammal in history to be cloned from an adult somatic cell.

At Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans in February 2025, this rapper's politically charged halftime show featured a full-band arrangement and a performance of his 2024 diss track that broke streaming records in the days that followed.

In January 2025, powerful Santa Ana winds drove fires through the Pacific Palisades and Altadena neighborhoods of this California city, destroying thousands of structures in what became among the most destructive fire disasters in state history.

In January 2025, this Chinese AI startup shocked Silicon Valley by releasing an open-source reasoning model that matched or outperformed leading American AI systems at a fraction of their reported training cost — triggering a sharp selloff in U.S. tech stocks.

Launched after the November 2024 election and directed by Elon Musk, this federal advisory body targeted government workforce reductions and spending cuts — its acronym shares a name with a Shiba Inu internet meme and a popular cryptocurrency.

During its January 2025 test flight, this SpaceX rocket's Super Heavy booster returned from its trajectory and was successfully caught for the second time by the launch tower's mechanical 'chopstick' arms — a key milestone toward fully reusable orbital spaceflight.

In 1998, these two sluggers — one in a Cardinals uniform, one in a Cubs jersey — captivated the baseball world chasing Roger Maris's 37-year-old single-season home run record of 61; one finished with 70 long balls, the other with 66.
questions.answer: Who are Mark McGwire and Sammy Sosa?

questions.question: On April 18, 1999, this NHL icon known as 'The Great One' played his final professional game — at retirement he held more records than any player in league history, and the league retired his jersey number across every franchise simultaneously.

This American cyclist won the Tour de France seven consecutive times between 1999 and 2005, having returned from a battle with testicular cancer — a story of triumph that unraveled when the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency stripped him of every title in 2012.

Selected first overall by the Philadelphia 76ers in the 1996 NBA Draft out of Georgetown, this 6-foot guard averaged 31.1 points per game in 2000-01, won the league MVP award, and became the shortest player in NBA history to receive that honor.

In the 2001 season, this San Francisco Giants left fielder clubbed his 71st home run to surpass a three-year-old single-season record and finished the year with 73 — a total that has never been officially broken, though his career was later clouded by a federal PED investigation.
